what_happened.line: The Planning Board approved a stormwater permit for 680 Reservoir Road by voice vote, with trash racks on both ends of the pipe and clearing limited to the driveway area.
The board approved a stormwater permit for 319 Highland Street by voice vote, with a condition to keep the culvert opening on the applicant's property clear.
The Highland Street hearing included long debate and abutter comment about town drainage discharging onto private property and a culvert that turned out to be private.
The board agreed to revise the Master Plan RFP to call for a broader public participation structure, and to table the driveways and entrances item until it has more members.
A prospective member was interviewed, and a joint meeting with the Select Board was set for the following Tuesday to make the joint appointment.

why_it_matters: Highland Street shows how drainage built by the town can end up on private land, leaving a homeowner to keep a culvert clear and nobody clearly responsible for the pre-existing problem.
The stormwater task force's staff-time logging is meant to estimate a dedicated funding mechanism, which could become a charge or budget request residents are asked to support.
The Master Plan RFP sets how much residents get to take part in the town's planning for the coming years.
watch_next: Joint meeting of the Planning Board and Select Board the following Tuesday, around 7:30 with a Zoom option, to appoint the new member.
The revised Master Plan RFP, and the DPW director's log of stormwater staff time for estimating annual capital outlay.

budget_items.topic: Sunny Hill Road right of first refusal purchase
budget_items.what_was_said: The 1.34 acres under the qualified offer carries a stated price the town could match. The board saw no reason to spend town money on landlocked wetlands.
A member noted town meeting had voted money for demolition of the old primary school.
One concept references a renovation cost for the existing hall.
The town will reimburse board members for training if they submit a paid invoice.

decisions.decision: Mr Jeffries will be invited to the November 14 meeting and the municipal building concepts will be the first agenda item.
Board members will read the municipal building concepts and discuss them at the next meeting.
Records storage was to be removed from the ongoing items list; the Brooks house memo will be emailed to the whole board.
Zoning near the Pond View comprehensive permit was to go under the comprehensive permit category, with a possible discussion on November 28.

what_happened.line: The Planning Board recommended in favor of the citizen petition to rezone part of 199 Mass Ave to commercial.
The board approved the 88 Mass Ave site plan with standard conditions, a sight triangle limit and set construction hours, after approving the requested waivers.
The board recommended approval of article 20, which would change motel use to a special permit.
The board recommended refusing the right of first refusal on parcel 3 Sunny Hill Road, seeing no reason to spend town money on landlocked wetlands.
The board approved three waivers for the warehouse site plan and continued that hearing to November 14 at 6:05 PM.

why_it_matters: The two zoning articles are warrant articles, so residents will be asked to vote on them at town meeting; the board's recommendations are advice and do not decide them.

The Sunny Hill Road recommendation bears on whether the town spends money on a purchase it could match, and the warehouse and municipal building items remain undecided and may come back with costs attached.
watch_next: November 14 meeting: the warehouse hearing resumes at 6:05 PM, and the municipal building concepts are the first agenda item.
A possible discussion on November 28 of zoning near the Pond View comprehensive permit.
